scope: Shared health and Windows/Unix lock implementation follow-up; read-only, no tests executed.

findings.detail: Shared health closes the sequential sibling-call case, but health is checked only before acquiring the global lock. B can pass the check and wait, then A writes a complete frame, fails Sync, poisons health and releases the lock. B acquires the lock and continues reading/writing without another health check. Constructors also perform IO without rejecting an already-poisoned supplied health.
findings.required: Check health after acquiring the global lock and before any journal IO, with correct unlock on rejection. Apply the same fail-closed rule to create/open. Preserve the pre-lock fast check if useful.
findings.regression: Use named barriers to prove B has passed its initial check and waits behind A before A's uncertain Sync failure. After acquisition B must return poisoned with zero further read/write/Sync success. Cover Snapshot, Transition and constructor use of poisoned health.

related_hardening: catalogHealthForTestOrSupervisor at line 101 silently creates a fresh health domain for missing, nil or multiple arguments. Make supervisor health an explicit required nonnil parameter; test helpers may construct their own domain. This prevents accidental same-supervisor bypass of the shared failure contract.
passed: The new shared health object uses a mutex and has no reset path; sequential sibling calls after poison reject.
Windows uses an exclusive LockFileEx byte range and Unix uses flock LOCK_EX with EINTR retry; each wrapper also serializes local goroutines and releases its local gate on lock failure.

Platform code is pilot_e2e plus platform build-tag isolated, receives existing handles and does not claim path/ACL verification. No additional independent blocker found in the basic lock implementation.
limitations: The new platform test only acquires/releases the same handle twice. It does not prove two-process exclusion, crash release, bounded waiting or verified identity.
Current sibling-health regression is sequential and does not cover the lock-wait race.
Lock timeout/termination supervision, bootstrap and case lifetime ownership remain future supervisor integration acceptance.
